title: Intune Sync now covers MDM and IME, with progress view
summary: In an Ignite-week post on 18 November 2026, Microsoft says the Windows Sync device action now starts check-ins for both the MDM client and the Intune Management Extension (Win32 apps, scripts, remediations), and that a Device sync status tab shows how far a sync got; per Microsoft Learn this applies to Windows and iOS/iPadOS and needs the 'Preview new device view' toggle. Push notifications now also cover IME workloads, so the 8-hour cycle is a maintenance cadence rather than the delivery time for every change. App inventory gains delta uploads several times a day, and report timestamps showing data freshness are still rolling out.
why: The 'wait eight hours' advice is wrong for most changes and wastes troubleshooting time. Knowing which client was asked to check in, and how fresh a report is, tells you whether a problem is delivery, processing or reporting.
todo: Turn on 'Preview new device view' in the Intune admin center and test Sync on a Windows pilot device; watch the Device sync status tab.
Update service-desk runbooks: one Sync now prompts IME too, so drop separate IME restart steps where they were only used to force a check-in.
Treat report timestamps as rolling out; until you see them, check 'Last checked' on app inventory before trusting a report.
effective_note: Mixed: improved Sync is documented on Learn (preview device view); report timestamps are 'rolling out' per Microsoft. Not verified in a tenant.
